title: Accounts Administrator
company: AMR - Specialist Property Recruiters - Agency - Permanent
description:
Full or Part Time Accounts Admin - Exeter 12-month contract £26,227 per annum, pro rata for part-time hours

We're recruiting on behalf of our client, a large property company in Exeter for an Accounts Administrator to support invoice processing and day-to-day accounts administration. This role would suit someone who enjoys working with figures, keeping records up to date and making sure details are entered correctly.

Invoice processing will be the main focus of the role. Day-to-day work is likely to include checking invoice details, entering information into the accounts system and following up where information is missing or unclear. You'll also support the team with general accounts administration and help keep invoice records organised. This is a 12 month contract but is likely to open other opportunities within the company for the right candidate.

Experience in financial admin, invoice processing or an administrative role involving figures and data entry would be useful. You'll be comfortable using computer systems, able to manage your workload and confident asking questions when something doesn't look right. Good attention to detail is particularly important when checking and entering invoice information.

Our client is open to appointing either one full-time person or two part-time people. For part-time applicants, the preferred working pattern is three days per week. Some home working is available once training is complete.

How to apply

Please send your CV to Fran Kent at AMR Recruitment and let us know whether you're interested in full-time or part-time hours. If you're applying for part-time hours, please include your preferred working days.

If this role is not suitable for you, but you know someone who may be interested, please ask about our £150 Recommend a Friend Scheme (subject to terms and conditions). We endeavour to speak with every applicant; however, due to the high volume of applications this is not always possible. To ensure your application receives full consideration, please highlight any relevant skills and experience within your application. If you have not heard from us within five working days, please assume that your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion and your data will not be retained.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Are you an experienced Accounts professional looking for a role that offers both flexibility and long-term stability? Join a growing business in a thriving manufacturing and distribution sector, where your finance expertise will be valued and where a 4 day working week is available (with up to 35 hours also considered).

Job Title: Accounts Assistant
Location: Cullompton, Devon
Salary: 28,000 - 32,000 FTE
Hours: 28 - 35 hours per week, worked across 4 or 5 days, with flexibility around start and finish times.
Benefits:

23 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, increasing by 1 day per year of service up to 28 days

Free on-site parking

4% employer contributory pension scheme

Join a thriving and resilient industry with excellent long-term career stability

The Company

Our client is a growing organisation within the manufacturing and distribution sector. They pride themselves on delivering high-quality products and maintaining strong relationships with both customers and suppliers. Due to continued growth, they are looking to recruit an Accounts Assistant to join their finance team.

The Role

This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and detail-focused individual to join a busy finance department. You will be responsible for managing the purchase ledger function, ensuring supplier invoices are processed accurately, maintaining supplier accounts, and supporting wider finance activities. The role also offers exposure to finance systems, reporting, reconciliations and cross-departmental support.

Key Duties
- Process supplier invoices, matching quantities, prices and VAT before posting to the accounts system.
- Investigate and report invoice discrepancies, liaising with internal stakeholders and suppliers.
- Monitor outstanding supplier invoices and proactively chase where required.
- Post overhead invoices and ensure payment deadlines are accurately maintained.
- Set up new supplier accounts and verify supplier bank details.
- Reconcile supplier statements and resolve any account queries.
- Process employee expenses and verify supporting documentation.
- Post supplier payments and issue remittance advice.
- Manage company credit card transactions and monthly reconciliations.
- Maintain accurate filing and record-keeping systems.
- Support environmental reporting requirements and provide holiday cover within the finance function.
- Assist with general administration and supplier-related enquiries.

Experience Required
- Previous experience working within a Purchase Ledger, Accounts Payable or Finance Administration role.
- Strong numeracy skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
- Strong organisational and communication skills.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a small team.
- A proactive approach and willingness to support wider business functions.

Interviews

Interviews will be taking place for this position on Wednesday 18th November.

How to Apply

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Location: Home-based with regular travel across Cornwall
Hours: 28 hours per week (Part-Time)
Contract: Permanent
Reporting to: Parish Finance Team Leader

About the Role

My client is seeking an organised and detail-oriented Deanery Bookkeeper to support a portfolio of parishes across Cornwall. This is a varied and rewarding role that combines bookkeeping, Gift Aid administration, training, and financial support for parish teams.

Working closely with Parish Priests, volunteers, and parish staff, you will ensure that financial records and Gift Aid processes are maintained accurately and in line with diocesan procedures. The role is primarily home-based but requires regular travel to parishes throughout Cornwall.

Key Responsibilities

Bookkeeping & Financial Administration
- Maintain parish accounting records using the Diocese's online accounting system (OPAS).
- Process receipts, payments, recurring transactions, and restricted funds.
- Reconcile bank accounts and cash records.
- Review financial information and identify any missing documentation or discrepancies.
- Support parishes in maintaining accurate financial records.

Gift Aid Administration
- Manage Gift Aid declarations and donor records.
- Process envelope allocations and cashless giving records.
- Reconcile Gift Aid and accounting records.
- Prepare annual Gift Aid returns and related documentation.

Year-End Reporting
- Prepare annual financial returns for submission to the Curia Finance Office.
- Respond to finance-related queries and provide supporting information.
- Assist parishes with annual donor communications and Gift Aid processes.

Parish Support & Training
- Provide guidance, training, and ongoing support to parish staff and volunteers.
- Respond to queries via phone, email, and in-person visits.
- Help ensure compliance with diocesan financial procedures.

Audit & Monitoring
- Carry out internal audits, year-end reviews, and financial monitoring activities.
- Complete risk assessment discussions and produce written reports where required.
- Work with parishes to resolve financial and procedural issues.

About You

We are looking for someone with excellent bookkeeping skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to build positive working relationships with a wide range of people. You will be comfortable working independently while managing multiple priorities across different locations.

Essential Requirements
- AAT qualification (full or part-qualified), equivalent qualification, or significant relevant experience.
- Previous bookkeeping experience.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams.
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently following initial training.
- Full driving licence and access to a vehicle for regular travel across Cornwall (mileage reimbursed).
- Commitment to ongoing learning and professional development.
- Sympathy with and understanding of the ethos and mission of the Diocese of Plymouth.

If you are an experienced bookkeeper looking for a flexible, part-time role where you can make a meaningful contribution to local communities, we would love to hear from you.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Are you an experienced payroll professional who enjoys working closely with clients and taking ownership of your work?

We're looking for a Payroll Administrator to join a friendly and collaborative payroll team, delivering accurate, reliable and responsive payroll services to a diverse portfolio of businesses.

This is a client-facing role where you'll have the opportunity to build strong relationships, manage your own portfolio and play an important part in ensuring payrolls are processed accurately and on time.

The Role

As a Payroll Administrator, you'll take responsibility for a portfolio of clients, working closely with them to deliver a high-quality payroll service while supporting the wider team.

What you'll be doing
- Processing a variety of client payrolls as part of a collaborative payroll team
- Acting as the primary point of contact for an allocated portfolio of clients
- Managing client payrolls from start to finish, ensuring accuracy and compliance
- Supporting the onboarding of new clients and payrolls, ensuring data is complete and accurate
- Identifying opportunities to improve processes, increase efficiency and enhance the client experience
- Building and maintaining strong, professional client relationships
- Responding to payroll queries accurately, professionally and within agreed timescales
- Keeping up to date with changes in payroll legislation and ensuring these are correctly applied
- Liaising with HMRC regarding employer payments and payroll-related matters
- Ensuring payroll deadlines are consistently met
- Working collaboratively with colleagues and providing support where required

About You

You'll be an organised and detail-focused payroll professional who takes pride in delivering an accurate and dependable service.

You'll ideally have:
- Strong knowledge and practical experience of UK payroll legislation
- Experience managing a portfolio of clients or multiple payrolls
- A proven track record of delivering excellent client service
- Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to your work
- Confident written and verbal communication skills
- The ability to build positive working relationships with a wide range of clients
- The ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a wider team
- Excellent organisation and time-management skills, with the ability to work to strict deadlines
- Good numerical and analytical skills
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Excel, Word and Outlook
- A professional, courteous and solutions-focused approach

What's on Offer?

You'll join an organisation that values its people and provides a supportive environment in which to develop your career.

Alongside a competitive salary, you'll have access to a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your financial, physical and mental wellbeing.

Financial wellbeing
- Employer-supported pension scheme
- Group life assurance
- Income protection
- Health cash plan, including support for eligible dependants

Mental wellbeing
- Confidential counselling and emotional support
- Virtual GP and second-opinion services
- Access to trained Mental Health First Aiders
- A range of resources to support your overall wellbeing

Physical wellbeing
- Cycle to work scheme
- Access to discounted gym, pool and fitness memberships
- Digital health and wellbeing resources
- Support and resources around menopause and women's health

Additional benefits
- Family-friendly benefits and enhanced family leave
- The opportunity to purchase additional annual leave
- Paid volunteering day each year
- Electric vehicle lease scheme, subject to eligibility
- Recognition of key career and family milestones
- Regular expert-led wellbeing webinars
- Access to charitable support for colleagues experiencing financial hardship

Why Join?

This is an excellent opportunity to join an established and forward-thinking professional services organisation where people are encouraged to develop, collaborate and make a genuine contribution.

You'll work alongside experienced payroll professionals, supporting a varied client base and gaining exposure to a broad range of payroll requirements.

The organisation offers a flexible approach to hybrid working, alongside a strong focus on learning, development, wellbeing and creating an inclusive working environment where people can be themselves.

If you're an experienced payroll professional looking for a role where client relationships, technical expertise and quality service are equally important, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to find out more.
